name: spreadsheet
title: Spreadsheet
description: The rows of a Google Sheet. Each row is read for the needs and products it holds; a row that holds none is set aside.

files.config.yaml:
# WHAT A PERSON SETS TO RUN THIS PIPELINE: the Import form, rendered by the canvas the way a
# node's config is. Only what the collect step does not know by itself: which sheet, which
# range. The credential is the node's, found by type in the org's store.
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [spreadsheetId]
  properties:
    spreadsheetId:
      type: string
      title: Spreadsheet
      description: >-
        The id from the sheet's URL, the part between /d/ and /edit. The sheet must be shared
        so that anyone with the link can view it.
      default: ""
      placeholder: 1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgVE2upms
    range:
      type: string
      title: Range
      description: >-
        The sheet to read, by name, or an A1 range such as Sheet1!A1:D100. The first row of
        the range is the header row.
      default: Sheet1
      placeholder: Sheet1
"ui:order": [spreadsheetId, range]
files.interface.yaml:
# A PIPELINE ON A CANVAS, as a node: the sheet may be named by an upstream node instead of
# the form, and its rows go downstream. The collect step's node carries its own credential,
# so this declares none.
inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: The sheet to read, as { spreadsheetId, range }, when wired from an upstream node instead of the form
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: rows
    type: array
    description: The inbox rows this run collected, one per sheet row, held until they are run
  - name: total
    type: number
    description: How many rows this run collected

credentials: []
files.pipeline.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
# A PIPELINE IS THE SOURCE SIDE: how content is collected and which objects it may yield.
# It never knows how an object is built; that is the object's own api/service.yaml. Between
# collect and the map sit the platform's steps, the same for every pipeline and every
# object: known, understand, make detail, match, retire, save (docs/unoverse/data/pipelines/README.md).
# A pipeline fills the collect slot and names its yields. It adds no step of its own.
type: pipeline
name: spreadsheet

# THE FACE, as a node's node.yaml carries it.
title: Spreadsheet
description: >-
  The rows of a Google Sheet. Each row is read for the needs and products it holds; a row
  that holds none is set aside.
whenToUse: >-
  Bring a sheet onto the map: a list of products, a register of requests, a table of
  offers, one thing per row, with a header row naming the columns. The sheet must be shared
  so that anyone with the link can view it. Every row lands in the inbox, held, until you
  run it.
category: Pipelines
version: 1.0.0
color: "#34A853"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1753618586/gravity/icons/googleSheetIcon.png

# COLLECT: one step, the sheet's rows, through the GoogleSheet node. The node carries the
# org's Google API key, found by type; nothing is repeated here. Headers are always on, so
# each row arrives keyed by its column names and the row can be read as "column: value".
collect:
  - name: sheet
    node: GoogleSheet
    config:
      spreadsheetId: "{{ config.spreadsheetId }}"
      range: "{{ config.range }}"
      useHeaders: true

# THE ROW each sheet row becomes. Every row of a sheet shares ONE source, the sheet's own
# address, so "same source, same title" matches within the sheet and a re-read of the sheet
# retires the rows it no longer holds (docs/unoverse/data/pipelines/README.md, the merge rule: "a
# spreadsheet by that sheet"). The row's own identity is its position in the sheet, which is
# what the known step compares on: an edited row is the same row changed, not a new one.
# The title is the first column; the text is every filled cell as "column: value", one per
# line, so the first sweep reads the row as the sheet's author laid it out.

# WHAT THIS PIPELINE MAKES: every row is read for its needs, and a row MAY be a product. A
# row is short, never a document. The two entries merge into one inbox item per row.
make:
  # EACH ROW, READ ONCE: one need (owner, 2026-09-13), and at most one product when the model
  # says the row is one.
  - each: "{{ collect.sheet.rows }}"
    sourceUrl: "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/{{ config.spreadsheetId }}"
    sourceId: "{{ config.spreadsheetId }}#{{ index }}"
    content:
      title: "return String(Object.values(item)[0] == null ? '' : Object.values(item)[0])"
      text: "return Object.entries(item).filter(e => e[1] != null && String(e[1]).trim() !== '').map(e => e[0] + ': ' + e[1]).join('\\n')"
    need: { cardinality: one }
    product: { cardinality: one, any: true }
files.test.yaml:
# THE PIPELINE UNDER GUARD: the collect step faked with a fixture sheet, the rows it yields
# asserted. Two sheet rows in, two inbox rows out, both addressed by the sheet, each
# identified by its position, the empty cell left out of the text, stamped with this
# pipeline's yields. The objects those rows become are the objects' own tests, not this one.
testData:
  config:
    spreadsheetId: sheet_fixture
    range: Sheet1
  fake:
    sheet:
      total: 2
      rows:
        - { Name: AQSAT Credit Card, Description: Shop now and pay in instalments with no interest., Fee: 0 }
        - { Name: Fees and charges, Description: null, Fee: 25 }
  expect:
    rows: "return output.rows.length === 2"
    source: "return output.rows.every(r => r.sourceUrl === 'https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/sheet_fixture')"
    identity: "return output.rows[0].sourceId === 'sheet_fixture#0' && output.rows[1].sourceId === 'sheet_fixture#1'"
    title: "return output.rows[0].content.title === 'AQSAT Credit Card'"
    text: "return output.rows[0].content.text === 'Name: AQSAT Credit Card\\nDescription: Shop now and pay in instalments with no interest.\\nFee: 0' && output.rows[1].content.text === 'Name: Fees and charges\\nFee: 25'"
    yields: "return output.rows.every(r => r.yields.join(',') === 'need,product')"
